kjv: A Syrian ready to perish [was] my father
mine: My father was a wandering Aramean
note: Hebrew 'arammi 'oved 'avi: 'oved can mean "perishing" or "straying, wandering" (of lost sheep), and the context (going down to Egypt as a sojourner) favours a homeless wanderer, i.e. Jacob; "Syrian" is an anachronistic label for Aram. Context: wandering (medium confidence). The creed continues 'he went down into Egypt and sojourned there': the life of a migrant, recalling Jacob's years in Aram.

kjv: neither have I taken away [ought] thereof for [any] unclean [use]
mine: nor removed any of it while unclean
note: Hebrew bitame' most naturally means "in a state of uncleanness" (parallel to be'oni, "in my mourning"); the KJV's supplied "use" shifts the uncleanness from the offerer to the purpose.

kjv: Thou hast avouched the LORD this day
mine: You have declared today that Yahweh is your God
note: Hebrew he'emarta (a rare hiphil of 'amar) means "you have caused to say / declared, affirmed" in a covenant exchange; "avouched" is obsolete.
